title: Ergodic topology sampling toward the continuum with Stochastic Normalizing Flows
summary: In this work we provide numerical evidence that topological freezing in $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory can be mitigated with a flow-based approach, as tested at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03~fm. We do so by analyzing the scaling of the costs of a computational strategy based on the combination of open boundary conditions and Stochastic Normalizing Flows. We show that the integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility remain under control throughout the explored parameter range with currently available computational resources. This marks an important step toward the use of even more efficient flow-based architectures for ergodic sampling of topology in state-of-the-art lattice gauge theory calculations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents numerical evidence that topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills theory can be reduced using a flow-based method, with the approach being effective at very fine lattice spacings. The costs and efficiency of this computational strategy, which uses open boundary conditions and Stochastic Normalizing Flows, are analyzed, showing controlled autocorrelation times and statistical uncertainties, thus paving the way for more efficient sampling in advanced lattice gauge theory calculations.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the challenge of topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills theory, which hinders ergodic sampling in lattice gauge theory simulations, by testing the effectiveness of a flow-based approach at very fine lattice spacings.
AI.method: The method involves the use of open boundary conditions combined with Stochastic Normalizing Flows to analyze the scaling of computational costs. The study measures the integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility across a range of parameters.
AI.result: The results show that the computational strategy keeps the integrated autocorrelation time and the statistical uncertainty under control, even at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03 fm, suggesting that the flow-based approach mitigates topological freezing effectively within the current computational resources.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion is that the flow-based approach, specifically using Stochastic Normalizing Flows, is a promising method for mitigating topological freezing, enabling more efficient and accurate lattice gauge theory calculations, and it opens up possibilities for further improvements with more advanced flow-based architectures.

title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Code available at https://github.com/Jianmu-lab/Jianmu-Q
summary: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.

AI.tldr: A new multi-agent framework, Jianmu-Q, has been developed to convert natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows, which was successfully tested on three increasingly complex field theories.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the challenge of translating continuum field theories into quantum computations, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems with a sign problem, in order to make use of the potential advantages of quantum computing for non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories.
AI.method: The method involves the development of the Jianmu-Q framework, which utilizes specialized agents for theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design. The framework includes physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations as part of its validation process.
AI.result: Jianmu-Q was benchmarked against three field theories, demonstrating that noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge to results from exact diagonalization and tensor networks. Additionally, selected circuits were run on IBM quantum hardware, showcasing an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion is that the Jianmu-Q framework effectively translates natural language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows, with successful validations and benchmarks, paving the way for further research and application of quantum computing in the field of quantum field theory.

title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
summary: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a lattice-QCD calculation of the hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) contribution to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment, using configurations from the ETMC. The results, with a 1% relative uncertainty, agree with other lattice groups and support the Standard Model prediction, which is consistent with the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment, while showing tension with data-driven dispersive determinations.
AI.motivation: To provide a precise determination of the HVP contribution to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric QCD, and to compare it with experimental data and other theoretical predictions, thereby testing the consistency of the Standard Model.
AI.method: The authors use gauge configurations from the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with four different lattice spacings and various quark mass parameters that match the definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD. They perform an extrapolation to the continuum limit and calculate the HVP contribution, including isospin-breaking corrections provided by the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper 2025.
AI.result: The calculated HVP contributions are $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. After adding isospin-breaking corrections, the full HVP value is $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$, which is consistent with the latest experimental result from the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment but shows tension with data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a robust and precise calculation of the HVP contribution to the muon's anomalous magnetic moment, supporting the Standard Model prediction and suggesting a need for further investigation into the discrepancies between lattice QCD and data-driven methods.
